terms.gloss: a man, as against a woman or a boy
evidence: Cic. Att. 5.1.3: tū invītā mulierēs, ego virōs accīverō
Cic. Tusc. 2.34: hoc puerī possunt, virī nōn poterunt?
terms.comment: A male person, the opposite of mulier and fēmina, and a grown man, the opposite of puer (Lewis & Short). Also a husband (see husband).

terms.gloss: a man, a fellow; properly a human being of either sex
evidence: Ter. Eun. 2.2.30: ibi homō coepit mē obsecrāre (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: In everyday speech “the man, the fellow” for someone just mentioned or not known (Lewis & Short); for people in general see human and people.

phrases.latin: Pompōnia, inquit, tū invītā mulierēs, ego virōs accīverō
phrases.english: “Pomponia,” he said, “you invite the women, and I’ll call in the men”

phrases.latin: ad eundem modum virō et mulierī et puerō datō
phrases.english: give it in the same way to a man, a woman and a child

phrases.latin: hoc puerī possunt, virī nōn poterunt?
phrases.english: children can do this, and men won’t be able to?

sources: Lewis & Short: vir · Lewis & Short: homo
